v.why: Replacing a skip connection on edge 0 with a 3x3 conv gives large gains (e.g. +43, +7 on C10), while replacing none or conv1x1 gives about zero.
Upgrading a skip on edge 4 to a 3x3 conv helps much more (+35 in the all-skip parent) than adding a conv where edge 4 is none or conv1x1 (about +0.5).
Replacing an avg_pool on edge 2 with a conv gives a large gain (+27 on C10 in observation 73), while edge 2 edits on other ops are near zero.
Swapping a weak avg_pool on the final edge for a 3x3 conv yields +6 to +15, more than from conv1x1 (+3 to +8) or from none/skip.
Removing edge 3 hurts most when edge 5 is already none, since the cell then loses its main path to the output (-78 and -21 on IN16).
When the direct edge 3 is absent, edge 2 (often a skip) becomes harmful, so removing it gives a gain (+11 on IN16) instead of the small loss seen with edge 3 present.
Downgrading a 3x3 conv on edge 0 to a skip loses accuracy (-11 to -17 in one parent), while replacing none or avg_pool with skip tends to help.
Removing a skip on edge 1 can help (+28 on C10 in the all-skip parent), while removing a conv on edge 1 reliably loses accuracy.
With edge 3 absent, a skip on edge 2 adds a useful route, giving a positive effect (+7 on IN16) where the same edit is neutral or negative when edge 3 is a conv.
Replacing a weak avg_pool on the direct edge 3 with a 3x3 conv gives large gains (+11.6, +16.7, +17.7), more than upgrading from conv1x1 or skip.

- **Weakest:** hypothesis 5 (edge 3 → none, condition edge 5 = none) rests largely on one very large observation (#53), and hypothesis 9 (edge 2 → skip_connect, condition edge 3 = none) is mixed on CIFAR-100.
